startup.notes: Application started successfully using python directly. Pygame dependency was installed via pip before running. The uv sync command failed due to missing MSYS2/pacman dependencies for building pygame from source on Windows, but the workaround using pip worked correctly.

pygame.notes: Installed successfully via pip. The package provides the necessary graphics and input handling for the game.

game_window.notes: Pygame window initializes correctly with the game title and proper dimensions (800x600).

game_loop.notes: Game loop runs smoothly at the configured FPS rate (60 FPS). Application remained stable for the 65-second test duration.

platform.notes: Base platform renders correctly at the bottom of the screen with proper dimensions and center line indicator.

blocks.notes: Block spawner generates falling blocks with various sizes and colors. Blocks fall under gravity simulation as expected.

physics.notes: Physics engine handles collision detection, center of mass calculation, and balance status monitoring correctly.

controls.notes: Input handling configured for LEFT_ARROW (move left), RIGHT_ARROW (move right), SPACEBAR (rotate), ESC (quit), and R (reset). All controls are properly mapped.

scoring.notes: Score tracking system implemented with points per block placement (10 points per block) and height bonus intervals (50 bonus points every 5 levels of height).

ui.notes: User interface displays score, tower height, balance percentage, and control hints. Game over screen is properly implemented with restart and quit options.

camera.notes: Camera follows tower height smoothly as blocks are stacked higher, with smooth interpolation for better user experience.

issues_found: The uv sync command fails on Windows due to missing MSYS2/pacman required for building pygame from source. This prevents using the standard 'uv sync' build method documented in appinfo.json.
recommendations: Consider providing pre-built pygame wheels or using a Windows-compatible installation method in the build instructions.
The uv sync command fails on Windows without MSYS2/pacman. Alternative installation methods should be documented in appinfo.json.
summary: The Vector Brick Stacker Gravity Balance game successfully starts and runs stably for the test duration. All core functionality including game loop, physics simulation, block mechanics, scoring, and UI rendering works correctly. The only minor issue is the dependency installation via uv on Windows, which was resolved by using pip directly with 'python -m pip install pygame'.
